$comment: THE ACCEPTED DEAD ACTIONS, EACH WITH THE REASON IT IS STILL HERE.
An action declared in a reducer union, handled by a case, and dispatched by no
production code is a feature the product cannot reach. Every entry below is one
of those, and every entry must say why it is tolerated.
This is a RATCHET, not a mute. tools/ci/reachability.test.mjs fails on an orphan
that is not listed here, AND on a listed entry that has since been wired - because
an entry that stopped firing is an entry somebody should delete.
Adding a row here is a decision. Write the reason for the next reader, not for the

accepted.reason: The pure camera arm. The board is @xyflow, which owns its own viewport and reports every move back as a whole viewport (Board.tsx -> onMove -> canvas/viewport), so no real camera change ever arrives as a delta. Kept because canvasReduce is deliberately written to be droppable into the store as one case block and the camera vocabulary is the model's. It becomes a gap the day the board needs a move the library does not originate.
Same as canvas/pan - superseded by canvas/viewport, which the library originates.

A node can be deleted by gesture and an edge cannot: BoardMenu targets nodes only, so the edge arm has no way in. RECORDED, NOT BUILT, and the reason is scope rather than difficulty - ReactFlow already exposes onEdgeContextMenu, so the work is widening BoardMenuTarget from a node shape into a union and giving the menu a second arm. That touches a sheeted surface with nine rendered tests for one small gesture, and it was ranked below the search surface and the local-first fix in the same pass. It is the cheapest remaining orphan and should be the next one taken.

BootSurface owns the pre-attach failure ladder inside its own hook and hands the store only the SETTLED outcome, so the store failure arm never fires from boot. The rail Retry rescan path restores previous graphs via repo/loaded + repo/stale rather than repo/failed. Recorded until an owner ruling deletes the arm or wires a true scan-failure surface.

DELIBERATELY DEAD, and it must stay that way. GRAPHITE-DECISIONS Decision 1 defers light and says not to tune light values; Graphite law 5 requires both themes at equal quality. Shipping a control that can select 'light' would ship an untuned theme. The state, reducer, persistence and data-theme stamp are all built and waiting on a ruling.

Owner seat-walk 2026-08-25 removed the rewrite control on sent user bubbles (no edit affordance on the prompt box). The reducer arm still rewrites history if something dispatched it; connect.tsx no longer does. Kept until an owner ruling deletes the arm or restores a different rewrite door.

The staleness endpoint. $comment: THE EXACT VOCABULARY THE SCANNER CAN SEE, ANCHORED BY NAME.
A floor cannot catch a SHRINK. Bounding the count at "> 50" let a refactor to a generic
action type hide five document actions while the total stayed at 82 - comfortably green,
and every hidden action would then have had to be deleted from the baseline as "no longer
an orphan". The route arm died the same way.
So the inventory is checked in by NAME. A name that disappears is reported as missing, and
updating this list is a deliberate act with a diff somebody reads.
